title: Generic methods and types

starter.Pair.java:
record Pair<A, B>(A first, B second) {
}

hints: `<T extends Comparable<? super T>>` lets `max` call `compareTo`, and also accepts types like `LocalDate` that are comparable with a supertype (`ChronoLocalDate`); this is how `Collections.max` is declared. `Collection<? extends Number>` accepts a list of `Integer`, `Double` or `Long`; `List<? super Integer>` accepts a list you can add `Integer`s to.

A `Map<K, V>` holds pairs from a key to a value (maps are covered fully in the next lesson). For `invert` you need only a few of its methods: `for (Map.Entry<K, V> e : map.entrySet())` visits every pair in the map's order, with `e.getKey()` and `e.getValue()`; `result.get(v)` gives the list stored for `v`, or `null` when there is none yet; and `result.put(v, list)` stores one. Create each group's list the first time you meet its value, then add the key to it.
